question: If you own a Nifty 50 index fund, you own a slice of each company's wage bill. Out of every ₹100 of that wage bill in 2025-26, how many rupees went to women?
discussion: Is the gap about what women are paid, or about who gets hired?

source.line: Nivel by The Equal Lens, from the companies' BRSR filings, 2025-26.
source.rule: Nivel's arithmetic, weighting each company by how much of it the index holds. 46 of 49 companies reported directly, 93% of the payroll. It mixes fewer women employed with lower pay per woman, and does not compare pay for the same job.

cite.saw: Women's share of pay (payroll you own) · FY26: 20.8%

question: A Nifty 50 index fund owns a slice of each company's wage bill, and women get less than half of it. Nivel splits that shortfall into two causes: fewer women employed, and less pay for each woman employed. Out of every ₹100 of the shortfall in 2025-26, how many rupees come from fewer women employed?
discussion: Which is harder to change: who gets hired, or what they are paid?

source.line: Nivel by The Equal Lens, from the companies' BRSR filings, 2025-26.
source.rule: Nivel's split of the gap to half the wage bill, using permanent staff and weighting each company by how much of it the index holds. 46 of 49 companies reported directly, 93% of the payroll. It does not compare pay for the same job.

cite.saw: 77% too few women employed, 23% women paid less on average (FY26)

question: The Nifty 50 includes five healthcare companies. Out of every ₹100 of their wage bill that a Nifty 50 index fund owns, how many rupees went to women in 2025-26?
discussion: Many people picture healthcare as women's work. What might explain this figure?

source.line: Nivel by The Equal Lens, from the companies' BRSR filings, 2025-26.
source.rule: Nivel's arithmetic, weighting each company by how much of it the index holds. All five reported directly. It mixes fewer women employed with lower pay per woman, and does not compare pay for the same job.

cite.saw: Sectors · FY26: Healthcare, women's share of pay 24.8%

question: The Nifty 50 includes four metals and mining companies. Out of every ₹100 of their wage bill that a Nifty 50 index fund owns, how many rupees went to women in 2025-26?
discussion: Why might metal and mining companies employ and pay so few women, and what would change it?

source.line: Nivel by The Equal Lens, from the companies' BRSR filings, 2025-26.
source.rule: Nivel's arithmetic, weighting each company by how much of it the index holds. All four reported directly. It mixes fewer women employed with lower pay per woman, and does not compare pay for the same job.

cite.saw: Sectors · FY26: Metals & Mining, women's share of pay 7.1%

question: In 2025, 80 FTSE 100 companies reported their UK gender pay gaps. In the average company, for every £1 a man earned an hour, how many pence did a woman earn?
discussion: If men and women get the same pay for the same job, why can the average gap still be large?

source.line: The UK government's gender pay gap service, averaged by Nivel by The Equal Lens, 2025.
source.rule: £1 less the average of each company's mean hourly pay gap, 13.0%, each company counting equally. UK staff only. It compares all men with all women, not pay for the same job.

question: In 2025, 80 FTSE 100 companies reported who sits in each quarter of their UK pay scale. In the average company, out of every 100 people in the best-paid quarter, how many were women?
discussion: Why are fewer women in the best-paid quarter than in the company as a whole?

source.line: The UK government's gender pay gap service, averaged by Nivel by The Equal Lens, 2025.
source.rule: Nivel's average of each company's share of women in its best-paid quarter, each company counting equally. UK staff only. Women were 41 of every 100 UK staff overall, averaged the same way.

cite.saw: Pay structure · 2025: women in the top pay quarter 33.2%

question: 146 ASX 200 companies report their Australian staff to the Workplace Gender Equality Agency. Weighting each company by its wage bill, out of every 100 people in the best-paid quarter of jobs in 2024-25, how many were women?
discussion: What would it take for the best-paid quarter to look like the whole workforce?

source.line: Australia's Workplace Gender Equality Agency, averaged by Nivel by The Equal Lens, 2024-25.
source.rule: Nivel's average of each company's share of women in its best-paid quarter, weighted by its Australian wage bill. Australian staff only, groups as they report. Women were 44 of every 100 Australian staff overall, weighted the same way.

cite.saw: Pay structure · FY25: women in the top pay quarter 33.6%

question: 152 Nikkei 225 companies report to a Japanese government database how many of their managers are women. In the average company's latest report, mostly for 2025, out of every 100 managers, how many were women?
discussion: What would need to change for more women to become managers?

source.line: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare database, averaged by Nivel by The Equal Lens.
source.rule: Nivel's average of each company's share of women among its managers, each company counting equally, using each employer's own definition of a manager. 143 of the 152 reports start in 2025.

cite.saw: Pay structure · latest: women in management 11.1%
